steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Place an oven rack in the center position. Lightly grease a 9x13-inch baking dish.

Bake sweet potatoes in the preheated oven on the center rack until a knife inserted into the centers easily glides through, about 35 minutes. Let cool enough to handle, then peel and mash in a large bowl.
Add eggs, sugar, 1/4 cup butter, heavy cream, vanilla, cinnamon, and salt to mashed potatoes; mix well and transfer to the prepared baking dish.
Combine remaining 1/4 cup butter, brown sugar, pecans, and flour in a medium bowl. Mix with a pastry blender or your fingers to the consistency of course meal. Sprinkle over sweet potato mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until topping is crisp and lightly browned, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Gourmet Sweet Potato Classic
raw_recipe.description: This unique sweet potato casserole features an irresistible brown sugar and pecan topping instead of typical marshmallows for a family-friendly side.

review.reviewBody: Now a tradition at our table! Thanks to all of the reviewers too - I heeded advice and cut back the white sugar to 1/3 cup and brown sugar to 2/3 cup which cut back on the sweetness. Hint for easy cooking of potatoes, just peel and then boil like regular white potatoes. No need to boil and them try to coax them out of their jackets the hard way :)

Excellent recipe, followed other users suggestions and added less sugar. I also used 2 big cans of yams instead of fresh potatoes (much less work) and replaced the cream with skim milk and I couldn't imagine it being better!

I halved the sugar in the potaoes, and it was still too sweet for my family. The topping was good though, but my husband said he'd rather have it on coffee cake. Easy to make and with some tweaking could be great, just not a recipe for us.

This is a winner at every Thanksgiving, especially for those who don't like the super-sweet marshmallow-topped casseroles that abound. I have made very slight alterations to how I prepare this one, based both on reviews I had read and personal preference. 

First for the ingredients (based on the 8-person serving size): I use 6 large yams, only 1 egg for a firmer texture, and just 1/4 cup white sugar. For the topping, I always make at least double the amount (so yummy - this really helps make the dish!!!). 

For the preparations: I peel, cut & boil the yams rather than baking them, as I have non-fire resistant hands and can't handle them for scooping after they've been in the oven! I also like to use a potato ricer to thoroughly break apart the boiled yams, into the mixing bowl. When I use my mixer, I throw away most of the "stringy stuff" that sticks to the beater, rather than scraping it back into the bowl. Though having used the ricer, there usually isn't that much waste. 

Aside from those minor things, this recipe is PERFECT!!! There are never enough leftovers, so sometimes I make an extra one to keep at home!

This is a great recipe -- however I did change it a bit. I boiled my sweet potatoes in sugar (brown) water with vanilla and butter. I then drained the water and followed most of the rest of the recipe with one additional change. I cut the white sugar in half and then mixed in approx. 1/4 cup brown sugar.

I cooked 4 whole large sweet potatoes in the Instant Pot, needing about 20 mins to be cooked and softened. Spooned out the pulp and added it to the eggs and dry ingredients (I used GF flour for as a friend has an intolerance); turned out great!! Did use less sugar, as recommended.

This dish was out of this world! I reduced the sugar to just 1/2 C of brown sugar. I left out the cream entirely by accident, but we didn’t miss it at all. And the topping I substituted crushed graham crackers in place of the flour. I made a very generous topping and completely packed it over the top of the casserole. It baked into a very nice and crunchy layer over the feather-light filling and just was delicious. My father in law asked for 3 helpings and he said he usually doesn’t like sweet potatoes at all! Our party finished the entire casserole at dinner. This will be my go to from now on.

Excellent recipe! I doubled it for a 9x13" pan but only used 3/4 c sugar overall. After baking the sweet potatoes in the oven for an hour I peeled, then mashed them in a bowl with the stated ingredients and used my immersion blender to get a creamy/fluffy consistency. I left the butter for the topping out to soften while the potatoes cooked. Mix your flour and brown sugar well before adding the pecans and keep adding the butter until the mixture is moistened but not oversaturated and then crumble on top by hand. I received many compliments on this dish and it tastes better than the one my mom has been doing for 30+ years!

I have never made sweet potatoes before. This was my first time and it was a hit with my family and guests! I am so happy that I cut the white sugar to 1/3 cup & brown sugar to 2/3 cup just as other’s suggested. Just so you would know (and not be alarmed), my sweet potatoes took much longer than 35 minutes to soften, it took more like 50 minutes to an hour, but that is OK, it was so easy to peel. I followed the recipe to the T! I’m impressed and will be making it time-and-time again!

This recipe is absolutely delicious! I’ve been making this for Thanksgiving and Christmas for several years now and it’s always a winner! Most people say it’s one of their favorite items on our expansive menu and ask for a copy of the recipe. I always double the amounts for the topping because my husband likes a thicker, crunchy topping. I use fresh sweet potatoes that I peel, cube, and boil before mashing, then mix in the other ingredients as listed. This is a MUST MAKE recipe! If you need to bring a dish to a holiday gathering and want to impress the guests, this is the dish to make!
Love it, but instead of baking them first I boiled them in apple cider!
I have been making this for years and years. Every time has been a success and I can’t imagine thanksgiving without this recipe.
I have made this for several years now for thanksgiving and never once have the sweet potatos been done baking in 35 minutes. Its always at least an hour, so keep that in mind.
I used an extra large can of Bruce’s yams instead of sweet potatoes, works great and skips step 2.
Been making this for years it is great and there is never any leftovers!
My family loves this recipe. I have to make it every year for the holidays.

I gave this 5 stars because my father-in-law (who has never said a positive comment about anything in 5 years) said this was the BEST sweet potato dish he's ever tasted. I don't like sweet potatoes and I made this dish for him and my husband. Everyone, including me and my 3 children really liked it. I've been changed by your recipe. Thanks for sharing with us all.*2024 Pop has since passed away, so I didn't make it last year. I heard all about it too. MUST HAVE!!

I just made this. I do like it but I think next time I'll cut the white sugar in half and add brown sugar to it. Also I made the topping with flour, brown sugar, and softened butter. Mix with a fork well then add chopped pecans. Very good!
I make this every year for the holidays! Everyone loves it!!! Thank you for the recipe!!
I make this 2 times a year, little if any leftovers
